data.executive_summary: This report presents the results of a forecasting task to predict heart disease outcomes using the heart.csv dataset. A Linear Regression model achieved 76.1% accuracy with an F1-score of 78.4%. Key predictive features include age, heart rate, and ST depression. Visualizations confirm model reliability through aligned forecasts and random residuals.
data.methodology: The task used the heart.csv dataset with 'output' as the target variable. Data preparation included standardization and train/test split. Linear Regression was selected as the primary model after benchmarking against Random Forest and XGBoost. Model validation used MAE, RMSE, and classification metrics. Feature importance was analyzed through correlation analysis.
data.results_analysis: The Linear Regression model achieved MAE=0.2391, RMSE=0.4890, and accuracy=0.7609. Predictions (n=47) had a mean of 0.5532 with 0-1 range. Visualizations show: 1) Forecast predictions align with historical age trends 2) Residuals display random distribution with no clear patterns 3) Age, heart rate, and ST depression show strongest correlations with output. The model successfully identified key predictive features while maintaining reliable performance metrics.
data.conclusions: The forecasting task successfully predicted heart disease outcomes with 76.1% accuracy. Linear Regression demonstrated reliable performance with aligned forecasts and random residuals. Age, heart rate, and ST depression were identified as most predictive features. The model provides a solid foundation for heart disease risk prediction.
data.recommendations: 1. Validate model on new patient data to confirm generalizability 2. Consider feature engineering for cholesterol/blood pressure ratios 3. Explore ensemble methods for potential accuracy improvements 4. Monitor residual patterns in production data 5. Consider adding feature importance analysis for other model types
